A Rishi, brother of Vasishtha and son of Mitra and Varuna;^* he is called <is>Maitravaruni</is> (“son of Mitra and Varuna”) and <is>Kumbhayoni</is> (“born in a jar”) (see below); he once saw his ancestors hanging in a cave, and was urged by them to procure progeny; he then from the most beautiful parts of all animals created <is>Lopamudra</is> and let her become the daughter of the king of Vidarbha; when he had married her he, in order to procure riches for her, applied successively to three kings, and then to the Danava <is>Ilvala</is>, who shaped his own younger brother into a he-goat that was digested by Agastya. Agastya had a son by Lopamudra named <is>Dridhasyu</is> or <is>Idhmavaha</is>. A. prevailed upon the <is>Vindhya</is> mountain to cease to increase in height “till he had returned from the South,” and drunk up the Sea (and digested it), in order that the gods might overcome the <is>Kalakeyas</is>.
